name: dark-baseline-r2
context:
SECOND SUBMISSION. YOUR OWN PIVOT WAS BUILT, MEASURED, AND IT DID NOT WORK. This brief exists because the standing requirement is that the baseline be BOTH proven by simulation and independently audited before being accepted as valid, and it has now failed the simulation twice.

═══════════ WHAT YOU RULED LAST ROUND ═══════════

Revision 1 was a single-shot aiming game in a seeded gravitational n-body universe: 12 bearings x 2 verbs = 14 named actions, one shot, steer a marked body into a marked ring. It failed 3 of 7 pre-registered gates, chiefly because only 3 of 24 seeded universes could be served -- an 87.5% rejection rate against a pre-registered band of 1-20%.

A coverage measurement separated the two candidate causes. With one shot the 14 actions produce 10.8 distinct landings and cover 33.7% of the target annulus; with two shots separated in time they produce 48.3 landings and cover 64.1%. The generator was innocent: one shot cannot aim.

You returned REVISE and refused the proposed patch: 'It is an admission. The One Shot Cannot Aim finding proves that the current discrete action lattice is mathematically incapable of satisfying a single-shot aiming objective... The design must either move to continuous control (which complicates the engine) or, more productively, pivot the objective from aiming to sequencing -- where the player uses the first shot to set the momentum for a second, more precise intervention.' Your headline: 'The baseline is currently attempting to solve a One Shot problem that the data has already falsified. The game, as currently structured, is actually a game of sequence and momentum management, not a game of single-action precision.'

═══════════ WHAT WAS BUILT AND MEASURED ═══════════

The game was rebuilt as a sequencing game, not patched: 14 actions x 2 shots = 196 sequences, 120 steps between them and 120 after, 5 bodies, 24 seeds. The horizon of 120 comes from a measured intuition-decay curve -- the angle between the bearing of a mass drop and the body's actual displacement is within 45 degrees on 100.0% of drops at 30 steps, 95.4% at 120, 67.6% at 360 and 42.6% at 600. The metric was changed to SHARE OF CEILING, the instrument the project's other two games are gated on, because a rank correlation over a single decision degraded into its own noise floor on a small sample in revision 1. The ceiling is the best of all 196 sequences and shares the player's action lattice exactly, so a negative solver margin would indicate a broken evaluator rather than a strong player.

The target zone is placed BLIND to which sequence wins -- a bearing drawn from the seed, at the median displacement distance -- and a seed is served only if at least two sequences reach it and doing nothing does not.

RESULTS:

  served by the viability oracle          14/24  (58.3%, up from 12.5%)
  mean ceiling score                      0.842
  AIM TWICE   share of ceiling            16.3%   aim, watch, aim again
  SPIN + AIM  share of ceiling            15.2%   YOUR policy: set momentum, then aim
  RANDOM      share of ceiling             9.7%   negative control
  ONE SHOT    ceiling, share of 2-shot    54.7%   same total time, best single action
  AGENCY      ceiling over doing nothing   0.842
  LIVE SEQUENCES within 10% of ceiling     3.6 of 196
  MOVE-VALUE ENTROPY                       5.30 bits
  COST BITE   budget changes the answer   42.9%

  H1 >=70% of seeds served                       FAIL  14/24
  H2 a human policy reaches >=50% of ceiling     FAIL  best of 16.3% / 15.2%
  H3 that policy beats random by >=15 points     FAIL  16.3% vs 9.7%
  H4 the 2-shot CEILING exceeds the 1-shot one   PASS  one shot reaches 54.7%
  H5 >=4 live sequences, and not all of them     FAIL  3.6 of 196
  H6 entropy >=4.0 bits over 196 sequences       PASS  5.30
  H7 agency over doing nothing >=0.30            PASS  0.842
  H8 cost changes the answer on >=30% of seeds   PASS  42.9%

NOT PROVEN, 4 of 8. Nothing was re-tuned to reach a pass.

═══════════ TWO THINGS THAT MUST BE STATED AGAINST MYSELF ═══════════

FIRST, A GATE OF MINE REPORTED A SPURIOUS PASS. H4 originally read 'intuition > singles OR singles < 0.9'. On the first run the clause it was actually asking about was FALSE (16.3% against 54.7%) and the second clause was true, so it printed PASS for a condition it was not testing -- and it compared incomparable things, an intuition-driven two-shot POLICY against a best single-shot CEILING. Rewritten to put a ceiling against a ceiling it passes for the right reason, and it is the one thing the sequencing pivot demonstrably bought.

SECOND, YOUR POLICY WAS IMPLEMENTED AND IT PERFORMED WORSE THAN THE NAIVE ONE. 'Spin first to set momentum, then aim from what the spin produced' reaches 15.2% of the ceiling; 'aim twice' reaches 16.3%. Both sit barely above a random control at 9.7%. The pivot is therefore not failing because of a bad implementation of your idea; the idea was implemented as specified and does not help. It was added AFTER seeing the first run's result, and the acceptance thresholds were deliberately NOT moved when it was added.

═══════════ THE AUTHOR'S READING, WHICH IS WHAT WANTS AUDITING ═══════════

The ceiling is rich -- 5.30 bits of move-value entropy, 3.6 live sequences out of 196, agency 0.842 over doing nothing, a cost that changes the answer on 42.9% of seeds. Every structural measure says there is a real game in there. And no rule a human can state reaches more than a sixth of it.

That is the exact inverse of a finding from game two, where exposing a forecast bought 31.6 points of agency floor by spending 47 points of solver margin -- it converted unreachable ceiling into reachable skill without creating skill, and the planner went from 63% to 88% of the ceiling. Here roughly 84% of the game is unreachable ceiling, a gap of the size that mechanic was measured able to move.

So the author's proposed next step is to stop treating the forecast cone as one factor among eight and treat it as the hypothesis: direction of effect is intuitive at 120 steps and magnitude is intuitive at no horizon, and these numbers say the unknowable half is most of the game.

questions.text: Your prescribed policy -- spin to set momentum, then aim -- was implemented and reached 15.2% of the ceiling against the naive aim-twice policy's 16.3%, both barely above a 9.7% random control. Does that falsify the sequencing pivot, or does it only falsify that particular two-rule policy?

A design with 5.30 bits of move-value entropy, 3.6 live sequences in 196, and agency of 0.842 over inaction, where the best human-statable rule reaches 16% of the ceiling: is that an undiscovered game or a demonstration that this substrate cannot carry a straightforward one?

The author wants to promote the forecast cone from a screened factor to THE hypothesis, on the argument that game two measured a preview-class mechanic moving numbers of this size. What is the strongest reason that reasoning is wrong?

One of my own gates printed PASS for a condition it was not testing, because of an OR clause, and I found it only by reading the output against the numbers. What cheaper instrument catches that class of defect -- a gate whose predicate does not match its name -- before a run rather than after?

Two designs, two failed proofs, and every failure recorded rather than re-tuned. At what point does continuing to revise this game stop being diligence and start being sunk cost, and what measurement would tell me I had reached it?
